label: Week 36, 2026
recap:
This week was quiet, with 15 bill movements and 10 case updates across 5 jurisdictions. California accounted for 7 of them, New York and the United States Congress had 3 each, and Delaware and Ohio had 1 each. Two bills carried no theme.

Children and minors led the themes with 4, covering companion chatbots, age verification, school use, and protections for people under eighteen. Employment and hiring, health care, and privacy and data followed with 3 each. Consumer protection and discrimination, deepfakes and likeness, elections, and infrastructure and energy each appeared once.

reading.body:
The week of August 31 to September 6, 2026 produced zero recorded activity in US AI policy or litigation: no bill movements, no court case updates, no federal filings.

A single week of silence in a legislative or regulatory record can reflect a recess, a filing deadline gap, or simply the limits of what the tracking system captures. The data does not distinguish between these possibilities, and no inference about a broader policy pause is warranted from one week alone.

What the data does not cover is as important to note as what it does. No bills, agencies, jurisdictions, or themes appear because none were logged, not necessarily because none existed. Readers drawing conclusions about the pace of AI governance should treat this week as a gap in the record rather than evidence of a trend.

themes.name: Children and minors
themes.blurb: Companion chatbots, age verification, school use, and protections for people under eighteen.

themes.name: Employment and hiring
themes.blurb: Automated screening of applicants, workplace surveillance, and decisions about pay or promotion.

themes.name: Health care
themes.blurb: Clinical decision support, utilization review, mental health chatbots, and AI in diagnosis or coverage decisions.

themes.name: Privacy and data
themes.blurb: Biometrics, training data, and what may be collected or fed into a model.

themes.name: Consumer protection and discrimination
themes.blurb: Algorithmic decisions that affect credit, housing, insurance pricing, or that produce unlawful bias.

themes.name: Deepfakes and likeness
themes.blurb: Synthetic images, voices, and video of real people, and who owns a likeness once a machine can copy it.

themes.name: Elections
themes.blurb: AI-generated political content, disclosure on campaign material, and interference with voting.

themes.name: Infrastructure and energy
themes.blurb: Data centers, the power they draw, and the local cost of hosting them.
